QF.id: SIA Logic Model for Social Programs_21

question.text: Bal Vikas Samiti's draft LFM lists the indicator 'Increase literacy rate for project beneficiaries'. Which revision makes it fully SMART?

answer.text: Increase literacy rate among 3,000 project beneficiaries (girls aged 10-14 in 40 villages of Bihar) from baseline 42% to 65% by 31 March 2027, measured by standardised ASER reading assessment
Increase literacy rate as much as possible
Increase literacy rate someday in the future

explanation.text: The Logic: SMART requires the indicator to be Specific, Measurable, Achievable, Relevant and Time-bound. Option A meets every criterion: Specific (3,000 beneficiaries, girls aged 10-14, 40 villages of Bihar), Measurable (42% to 65%, ASER assessment), Achievable (a 23-point lift over the stated period is plausible), Relevant (literacy outcome aligned with the project) and Time-bound (by 31 March 2027). The Trap: Option B uses a qualitative adverb ('significantly') with no measurable target. Option C has no ceiling. Option D is untimed. All three fail at least one SMART criterion. Note: A simple five-tick SMART checklist applied to each draft indicator catches vague wording before it reaches the AIR.
